title: Exact completion functor and its canonical triangle comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with uniformizer $\pi$, and $X$ any scheme. Work in $D(R)$ for $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, with the coefficient category of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] and localization $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an unbounded complex $M$ take the strict reduction tower $D_\bullet(M)$, its transitions and maps $j_n$ of [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus], and apply the Roos functor $H$ of [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]. The formula $F(QM)=QH(D_\bullet(M))$ descends to an additive endofunctor $F:D(R)\to D(R)$, and
$$c_M(m)=(((m,0))_{n\ge1},0)$$
descends to a natural transformation $c:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow F$ which is the canonical completion map of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] up to isomorphism: for every $K\in D(R)$ there is an isomorphism from $F(K)$ to the derived limit $R\varprojlim_nK_n$ specified there, under which $c_K$ corresponds to the specified canonical map $K\to R\varprojlim_nK_n$. In particular $K$ is derived complete if and only if $c_K$ is an isomorphism. There are coherent natural comparisons $\sigma_{K,r}:F(K[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(K)[r]$ for all $r\in\mathbf Z$, satisfying $\sigma_{K,r}c_{K[r]}=c_K[r]$. For every distinguished triangle $T=(K\xrightarrow{f}L\to C\xrightarrow{w}K[1])$, its image $F(T)$, whose last arrow is $\sigma_{K,1}F(w)$, is distinguished, and $(c_K,c_L,c_C):T\to F(T)$ is a morphism of triangles, including its last square with $c_K[1]$.

proof.text: Write $G(M)=H(D_\bullet(M))$ on complexes. By [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus], $D_\bullet$ is a strict additive tower functor and sends a quasi-isomorphism to a levelwise quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus], $H$ is additive and sends such tower maps to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus $G$ is additive and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The compatible maps $j_n(m)=(m,0)$ satisfy $t_nj_{n+1}=j_n$. Consequently the augmentation clause of the Roos lemma gives the natural chain map $c_M(m)=(((m,0))_n,0)$. In particular this specifies the zero homotopy of $(1-T)(j_n)_n=0$; it is not a choice of a lift inside the triangulated category.

Apply Mathlib Localization.lift and Localization.fac to QG, which inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Descend Q of the strict augmentation with Localization.liftNatTrans; liftNatTrans_app gives c(QM) followed by the descent isomorphism equal to Q(a_M). These are exactly the universal-property clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] for the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: The assembled tower is additive by evaluation at every tower index and complex degree, using [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus]. The Roos functor is additive by [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]. Transfer additivity across FQ ≅ QG. Factor Q through the homotopy quotient and Qh: Functor.additive_of_full_essSurj_comp descends it past the homotopy quotient, and Localization.functor_additive_iff descends it past Qh. Thus F is additive.

Assemble the supplied coherent shifts of D_n degreewise into coherent shifts of the tower, using transition compatibility from [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus]. Compose with the Roos coherent shifts from [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]. Its ShiftAugmentation and AugmentationNaturality equations give a(M[r]) followed by the composite shift isomorphism equal to a(M)[r]. Mathlib Functor.commShiftOfLocalization and NatTrans.commShift_iso_hom_of_localization descend the shifts and descent isomorphism through [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. To descend augmentation compatibility, precompose with Q and cancel the invertible Q-shift and descent maps; naturality and the two known shift equations give the desired equation.

Work directly in the internal module category used by [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], with its actual tensorRight functors, quotient objects and levelUnit maps. The existing [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution] and [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] supply functorial flat resolutions for the sheaf and internal-module categories. The adopted source CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_flat_kFlat, attached to [lem-sfb-abstract-kflat-resolution], then supplies flat K-flat replacements in this Grothendieck monoidal category. No change of encoding to ringed-site section modules is required. For each quotient use the actual map levelUnit and the scalar action pinned sectionwise by [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus].

proof.text: Pull the exact coefficient short complex of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] to X and transport its regular module to the tensor unit by regularPullbackIso. The canonical scalar of [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus] equals the recorded uniformizer power by checking its action on sections. Tensoring with flat terms preserves this short exact sequence. Mathlib mappingCone.quasiIso_descShortComplex, the declaration of [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso], proves that its cone-to-tensor quotient map is a quasi-isomorphism for flat complexes. For an arbitrary K-flat P, replace P by a flat K-flat complex P′: scalar cones preserve that quasi-isomorphism by the cone triangles and two-out-of-three, tensorRight preserves it by MorphismProperty.whiskerRight_of_kFlat, and naturality of descShortComplex transfers the assertion to P. The coordinate formulas prove strict transition compatibility and that each j_n maps to levelUnit.

proof.text: Obtain CountableAB4Star for internal pro-etale module sheaves from the adopted proved Mod.epiπAppZeroOfEpi and Scheme.ProEt.epi_π_app_zero_of_epi_addCommGrpCat, hence use [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus] on the assembled tower. Its levelwise quasi-isomorphism theorem and augmentation naturality carry the strict cone-to-tensor tower map to a quasi-isomorphism preserving augmentation. Compare that tensor tower directly with the complex roos in [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]: degreewise use the biproduct isomorphism (v,u) ↦ (v,−u), together with the product isomorphism induced by identical levels. The published differential coordinates verify it is a chain isomorphism; it fixes the zero-second-coordinate augmentation. Localize this explicit isomorphism. For any representative e:QP ≅ K, compose F(e inverse), the descent isomorphism, and this comparison. Naturality of c proves its composite with c_K is exactly completionMap. The specified isDerivedComplete_iff and existence of a flat K-flat representative then give completeness iff c_K is invertible.

proof.text: For any chain map f, evaluate at each tower index. The supplied transition-compatible cone isomorphisms from [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus] assemble to an isomorphism D_bullet(Cone(f)) ≅ Cone(D_bullet(f)); evaluation commutes with mapping cones, their inclusion and signed boundary. The inclusion and boundary clauses of that calculus make it an isomorphism of cone triangles after using the assembled tower shift comparison. Apply the Roos mapTriangle functor and compose with its boundary-preserving cone-triangle isomorphism from [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]. Thus G sends each ordinary cone triangle to one isomorphic to the cone triangle of G(f). By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], localizing the latter gives a distinguished triangle. The specified augmentation at the third vertex is the same natural augmentation already constructed; step 9 proves its triangle squares directly from naturality and shift compatibility, so no separate cone-augmentation identity is needed.

By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], any distinguished triangle $T$ is isomorphic to the image of a chain-map cone triangle. Applying $F$ and the natural shift comparison carries that isomorphism to an isomorphism of image triangles. Step 8 and closure of distinguished triangles under isomorphism show that $F(T)$ is distinguished. The first two squares for $(c_K,c_L,c_C)$ are the naturality equations for $c$. For the last square write its last arrow as $w:C\to K[1]$. Naturality gives $F(w)c_C=c_{K[1]}w$; multiplying by $\sigma_{K,1}$ and using step 4 gives $\sigma_{K,1}F(w)c_C=c_K[1]w$. This is exactly the required last triangle square, including the prescribed boundary sign. Thus all three components form the asserted morphism of distinguished triangles.

lean.statement: theorem completion_triangle_comparison : ∃ data : PrincipalReductionConeData l E X, data.IsCanonical l E X ∧ ∃ (a : 𝟭 (CochainComplex (Modules l E X) ℤ) ⟶ complexCompletion l E X data) (F : DerivedCategory (Modules l E X) ⥤ DerivedCategory (Modules l E X)) (c : 𝟭 (DerivedCategory (Modules l E X)) ⟶ F) (κ : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ F ≅ complexCompletion l E X data ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) (sF : F.CommShift ℤ), F.Additive ∧ (∀ (M : CochainComplex (Modules l E X) ℤ) (p : ℤ), (a.app M).f (p + 1) ≫ (roosχ ((tower l E X data).obj M) p).hom = biprod.lift 0 ((Pi.lift (f := fun n : ℕ ↦ ((tower l E X data).obj M).asFunctor.obj (op n)) (fun n : ℕ ↦ (data.j n).app M)).f (p + 1))) ∧ (∀ M : CochainComplex (Modules l E X) ℤ, c.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) ≫ κ.hom.app M = DerivedCategory.Q.map (a.app M)) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Modules l E X)) (P : CochainComplex (Modules l E X) ℤ) (_hP : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (Modules l E X) (.up ℤ)).kFlat P) (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ K), ∃ ψ : F.obj K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (AdicCompletion.roos l E X P), c.app K ≫ ψ.hom = completionMap l E X K P e) ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Modules l E X), IsDerivedComplete l E X K ↔ IsIso (c.app K)) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Modules l E X)) (r : ℤ), c.app (K⟦r⟧) ≫ (Functor.commShiftIso (self := sF) F r).hom.app K = (c.app K)⟦r⟧') ∧ (∀ (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (Modules l E X))) (_hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (Modules l E X))), Triangle.mk (F.map T.mor₁) (F.map T.mor₂) (F.map T.mor₃ ≫ (Functor.commShiftIso (self := sF) F (1 : ℤ)).hom.app T.obj₁) ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (Modules l E X)) ∧ ∃ γ : T ⟶ Triangle.mk (F.map T.mor₁) (F.map T.mor₂) (F.map T.mor₃ ≫ (Functor.commShiftIso (self := sF) F (1 : ℤ)).hom.app T.obj₁), γ.hom₁ = c.app T.obj₁ ∧ γ.hom₂ = c.app T.obj₂ ∧ γ.hom₃ = c.app T.obj₃)
